Where · when · what geometry

A force-carrying
geometric excitation

Construct one admitted wavepacket, emit it from a finite source, calculate its overlap force on a receiver, and absorb it with a complete energy and momentum account.

Selected construction. Extend the existing internal wave across a spatial channel. The resulting excitation has its own dynamics, positive energy, translation momentum and the retained spin property. Granularity admits a complete packet; an explicitly extended collapse law transfers it from a source to the channel and from the channel to a receiver.

The source assumptions and additions are fixed before calculation. The conservation-to-instantaneity inference is audited in §11. Sections 12–16 construct the packet and its complete interaction. Section 17 gives the solved numerical example; §18 states exactly when the geometry changes, the receiver responds and the record is written.

01 / Scope

One complete emission, flight and absorption, and what conservation requires of the update at once

Question. Can D2's internal wave, extended across one spatial channel, form an admitted packet that a finite source emits, that exerts a calculated overlap force on a receiver and that the receiver absorbs, with granularity and collapse doing specified work and the complete energy, momentum, action and spin closed at every point (§9)? And for the clock-and-ruler update at once that the construction keeps, D4 premise 6: what do its two conservation arguments establish (§11)? G1, C1, GA1, D2, D3, D4 and D5 are the citation keys of the source table in §9; their documents and the passages used are listed in section 4.

Result. Under the declared premises, the construction produces one elementary admitted, localized, independently evolving excitation that carries energy, momentum and the retained internal spin, exerts a calculated overlap force, and is emitted and absorbed with complete conserved balances. It meets the particle criterion fixed in §13 (Verdicts). At every point of the process, including both events, the action, spin, energy and momentum totals are

FC50
\[Q_E^{\rm bound}+Q_c+Q_R^{\rm bound}=Q,\qquad \mathbf{S}_E+\mathbf{S}_c+\mathbf{S}_R=\frac{Q}{2}u^\dagger\boldsymbol{\sigma} u.\]
FC51
\[H_E+H_R+E_c+U_R=H_E^{\rm initial}+H_R^{\rm initial},\qquad P_E+P_R+P_c=0.\]

For the update at once, §11 establishes four results.

  • Steady upkeep. Within D4's inventory, continual net outward light cannot maintain the unchanged pull of an unpowered steady source. By FC01 a continuing positive net outward energy current lowers the enclosed energy, and under D4's flux/count relation the pull falls with it; D4 premise 1 gives a time-invariant gravitational force between the two Gaussian surfaces when nothing crosses the source's surface.
  • The no-emission split. Momentum conservation and the specified forces on the halves require the present-configuration pull \(+Kq\) on the still body at each \(T\), exactly at the stated positions and to first order in the pulls for free motion. Every departure from \(+Kq\), including a partial or late response, leaves momentum unbalanced by the amount of the departure. To that order the result extends to each eligible still probe and, with the clock step applied at each \(T\), to the rates of clocks held at rest.
  • The circular trial. For two equal bodies on a circle, each pulled toward where the other was one light-travel time earlier, \(\dot E=2vQ\sin\delta\) and \(\dot L=2aQ\sin\delta\) with \(\delta=(v/c)\cos\delta\). With no other energy or angular-momentum entry, conservation excludes that late law in this configuration.
  • Bodies that move. If the complete energy, apart from constant rest energy, is \(\sum_iK_i+U(q_0,q_1,\ldots,q_m)\), with \(U\) differentiable and counted once, and the sampled position rates can vary independently at fixed sampled positions, the work law and energy conservation require the potential to depend only on the present configuration, a pull that depends only on those positions to be its negative gradient, and any velocity-dependent remainder that is finite at zero present velocity to have zero summed power (FC58).

Beyond these conditions, and for the rulers around a moving count, the rule is stated in D4 premise 6. In the constructed process the receiver experiences an immediate tail force and writes its terminal record at \(T_A=45.9015912014\,\tau_0\) (§18).

ElementSpecification
SystemA source body E, a receiver body R and the carrier between them on one flat spatial channel. Each body has a centre coordinate and momentum, a bound internal excitation slot, C1's scalar oscillator (its buffer) and a stable record (FC-APP, FC26, FC39). The carrier is D2's internal wave extended across the channel, \(\varphi(x,U,T)\) on the channel and \(K=SU(2)\), written through the coefficients \(b_n\in\mathbb{C}^2\), \(n\in\{-N,\ldots,N\}\) (FC09). In §11: an unpowered source between two Gaussian surfaces, the no-emission split, two equal bodies on a circle, and any number of bodies that move.
DomainD2's lowest internal doublet in its positive-frequency sector; complete packets of the enlarged finite family (FC-SECTOR); a nonnegative window bounded by one and \(0\lt\varepsilon\lt1\) (FC25); the source-capacity and capture domains FC38 and FC47 with a nonzero capture anchor (FC43); collinear motion, with the internal spin polarization fixed during spatial coupling (§10).
PreparationThe emitter at rest with one bound excitation \(a_E^\dagger a_E=Q=s_*\), a ready record and no carrier excitation, with an isotropic source overlap \(-\kappa_E\omega_0Q\), \(0\lt\kappa_E\lt1\) (FC33); the receiver at rest with a ready record and an empty bound slot; the constants of §17. A control trial has no prepared source excitation (§18).
Observers, clocks and rulersOne common time \(T\) on the flat channel, the time that the frames with no force share (D4 premise 6), with the channel coordinate \(x\) of the common flat comparison frame. Each event updates the complete configuration on one \(T\) slice (C-TIME). Each body's oscillator runs on that body's proper clock (FC41). Units \(s_*=\omega_0=c=1\) (FC52). In the split, the clock rate of clocks held at rest is normalized to one at infinity.
BoundariesA periodic channel of length \(L\): a specified calculation domain and a flat translation-channel idealization, not a bent physical ring. Smoothness on \(K\). The interaction ends well before the packet wraps around the period. In the steady-upkeep argument, the source's Gaussian surface and the observer's surface outside it.
Approximation levelThe finite-band Hamiltonian and the event accounting are exact; FC29–FC32 and FC45–FC51 are analytic. The trajectory is numerical, with the tolerances and refinement of §20. The split's force evaluation is exact at the stated positions and holds to first order in the pulls for free motion; the probe and the held clocks hold to the same order. FC58 and its two branches are exact under their stated conditions.
What decides itEach result is fixed by its displayed equations. A conservation residual above the stated tolerances, a failed capacity inequality FC38 or FC47, a zero capture anchor or a violated bound FC25 would refute the worked process; the checks of §20 and the tables of §17 test exactly these. In §11 the decisive quantities are the displayed energy rate, force sums and power.

1.2 Common obligations that do not apply

These checks are often requested of a force carrier. None follows from a claim this document makes or from a premise it adopts.

CheckWhy it does not follow here
Identify the carrier as a photon, a graviton or a member of a universal family of force particlesThe construction “derives a model carrier for the selected overlap interaction” and makes no such identification (§10).
Supply a measurement, commutator, spin-statistics or quantum-field structureNone is inherited (§10). The phase evolution is derived from the canonical form without a commutator rule (§12), and the spin-½ representation “supplies no exchange-statistics requirement” (§13).
Solve unrestricted three-dimensional orbital motion and boost transportThe claims are made on one collinear spatial channel; these lie outside this calculation (§13).
Prove a strict signal frontNo signal-front claim is made: “a monochromatic group velocity alone is not a signal-front theorem”, and the registration time is set by the threshold law (§18).
Model noise, instrument resolution or a continuously monitored force readoutThe record protocol is an explicit terminal-record protocol, and the claim is the record channel completed at \(T_A\) (§18).
Derive a Born probability for captureOnly one terminal channel is supported; its weight is one, and the anchor supplies a phase (§16).
Preserve every spatial-mode invariant at captureFC-TRANSFER resets the spatial mode ratios as specified; the document does not claim to preserve every spatial-mode invariant (§16).
Show a soliton or a universal lifetimeNone is presumed. The packet may disperse while preserving its action and energy, and its broadening is calculated (§13, §17).
Produce decay products, a decay rate or a lifetimeFC57 is an interface only; “Separate internal-space collapse causes decay” remains the reserved hypothesis (§19).
Include the packet's gravitational self-interaction or a curved channelThe laboratory is flat and local with negligible gravitational self-interaction, and periodicity is a flat translation-channel idealization (§10).
Complete the reconciliation of spin and curvatureA separate task (§19), carried by “Granularity, Collapse, Spin and Curvature”.
Compress every continuum wave exactlyThe bounded refinement supports the displayed trajectory (§20).
Provide new empirical validationNone is claimed (§10).
Derive the widths and coupling strengths from granularityGranularity does not determine them; they are named inputs (§10).
Use D4's moving two-body energy statement as an exact many-body HamiltonianThat statement is first order and is not used as one; the construction supplies its own complete flat-laboratory Hamiltonian (§11).

02 / Method

A finite route from one wave action to a written record

The calculation follows one finite chain. It extends D2's internal wave across a spatial channel and varies the action, which gives the modes and the conserved charges. G1's admission fixes the packet's total action. The receiver couples to the packet through minus \(\varepsilon\) times the overlap of its window with the packet's actual canonical energy, and the force on the receiver follows from how that overlap changes with the receiver's position (FC27). The source emits the whole packet in one complete event when its accumulated overlap action reaches the threshold; the packet and the receiver then evolve under one Hamiltonian; the receiver captures the packet in a second complete event at its own threshold. The balances close analytically at every point, and the solved interaction checks them in numbers. Separately, §11 takes the two conservation arguments of D4 premise 6 and calculates what each establishes.

Held fixedThe total admitted action \(Q=s_*\) (FC30, FC50); the internal polarization \(u\) (§16); the bare body energies; the channel length \(L\), the band \(N\), the window width \(a_w\) and the strength \(\varepsilon\); the body positions during each instantaneous event (FC35, FC45).

2.7 Diagnostic examples, kept distinct

The two-mode force FC28 checks the sign and the nonvanishing of the force; the trajectory uses all retained modes. Twenty-four independent complex-state and translation samples check covariance and the continuous conservation derivatives. The no-source trial is the exact zero-field control. The N = 96 run checks the band. These examples check the general results; they do not replace them. The general statements are analytic: FC25 for every retained finite spatial family, FC29–FC32 and FC45–FC51 in the active finite Hamiltonian model, and FC58 under its stated conditions.

03 / Premises

Every material input, with its status

The register lists the inputs the calculation actually uses, each with its exact statement, status, domain, provenance, uses and appendix. Definitions, root physical premises, imported results, new completions, preparations, a calibration, an empirical datum and a comparison-only assumption are kept distinct. A result proved elsewhere enters as an input, and its own upstream premises stay part of its dependency contract (section 4). The additions FC-WAVE to FC-TRIGGER are “provisionally adopted, then checked by their consequences”, and with the retained inputs they form “one sufficient conditional completion” (§10), not a unique derivation.

The dependency graph

The graph is finite, and every chain ends at an identified root.

  • Roots. D4's conservation laws and work law, with its measured constants \(G\) and \(c\) (FCE-P18, FCE-P19); D4 premises 1, 3, 5 and 6 (FCE-P15–FCE-P17); D2's registered premises, among them M1 and G2 (FCE-P02, FCE-P03); G1's admission law and CAL (FCE-P05, FCE-P06); C1's additions (FCE-P07); the definitions taken from GA1, D3 and D5 (FCE-P04, FCE-P24, FCE-P25); this document's completions (FCE-P08–FCE-P14), conditions and preparations (FCE-P20, FCE-P21, FCE-P26–FCE-P28); the particle criterion (FCE-P23); and the trial law under test (FCE-P22).
  • Edges. D2 → G1 → this document; D2 → C1 → this document; G1 → C1, whose event acts on packets that G1's tensor admits; D4 → C1, whose C-TIME extends D4's ordering to collapse; D4 → this document (§11, FC03, FC04 and the common \(T\)); GA1, D3 and D5 → this document.
  • No circle of support. “Granularity, Collapse, Spin and Curvature” is downstream: it uses this document's carrier, and this document cites it only for the separate reconciliation. The carrier's equations FC05–FC57 are one jointly defined system, solved together.
05 / Appendices

One appendix for each premise

Each appendix states its premise, its upstream inputs, its foundation or derivation, its domain and status, and links back to the premise and the obligations that use it. An adopted input (a root physical premise, an imported result, a completion, a definition, a preparation, a calibration or a datum) is identified as an input, and the checks and consequences that this document calculates for it are shown. Where the document derives a consequence, its own equations and words are transcribed. Key equations stay visible; longer material is in the expandable blocks.

FCE-A01 · D2's internal geometry (for FCE-P01, part of “Retained D2 / G1”)

Premise FCE-P01 · imported proved result · used for FCE-O01, FCE-O02, FCE-O13

\[-\Delta_K\phi_\pm=3\phi_\pm,\qquad \omega_0^2=3\Omega^2.\]

Statement. The internal space is \(K=SU(2)\) with its round geometry and right character \(k=1\). The retained internal ground modes obey the displayed relations (§12). The canonical variables are positive-frequency, the full coefficient phase is kept, and “The original positive-frequency preparation remains an explicit sector choice” (§10).

Foundation, the step used here, and the checks made

Upstream inputs. D2's registered premises for its specified internal geometry.

Foundation. D2 calculates the admitted spectrum from the selected winding sector: the two lowest modes, their normalization and their gap to the next sector, with a completed-square proof of the energy minimum at fixed positive action (D2, “Why exactly two lowest modes remain”). This document does not repeat that proof.

Step used here. With these modes and the internal term \(-\Omega^2|\nabla_K\varphi|^2\) of FC05, the variation gives the frequencies \(\omega_n=\sqrt{\omega_0^2+v^2k_n^2}\) of FC06, and \(Q\omega_0\) is the modal gap energy that \(E_c\) already contains (§13).

Checks made here. “Every \(b_n\) belongs to D2's same lowest internal doublet” (§19). The common-polarization form \(b_n=\beta_nu\) is preserved by the spin-independent spatial dynamics (§16), and the energy overlap is the identity on the doublet (§19). Symbolic check 8, “smooth_internal_spin”, passes (§20).

FCE-A02 · Energy and inertia, D2's G2 (for FCE-P02)

Premise FCE-P02 · imported proved result of D2 under its completion G2 · used for FCE-O01, FCE-O07

FC07
\[E^2=(Q\omega_0)^2+v^2P^2,\qquad E=Q\omega_0+\frac{P^2}{2(Q\omega_0/v^2)}+O(P^4).\]

Statement. “D2's G2 identifies the free internal energy with inertial mass through E/c²” (§10); “D2 G2 assigns the same free internal mode inertial mass \(Q\omega_0/c^2\)” (§12). Conclusion used here: \(v=c\) for this branch.

Hypotheses, the document's derivation of \(v=c\), and further uses

Upstream inputs. D2's motion completion G2, “Vary the proper-time internal action with respect to the center trajectory; no additional acceleration or curvature term”, and D2's calculation in “Its energy supplies inertia and gravitational response”.

Derivation in this document (§12). For a pure mode of action \(Q\) the energy and translation charge are \(E=Q\omega\) and \(P=Qk\). With FC06's dispersion this gives FC07, whose low-momentum inertial coefficient is \(Q\omega_0/v^2\). Matching it to D2's \(Q\omega_0/c^2\) fixes \(v=c\):

FC08
\[\omega_n=\sqrt{\omega_0^2+c^2k_n^2},\qquad v_g(k)=\frac{c^2k}{\omega(k)},\qquad \omega-kv_g=\frac{\omega_0}{\gamma_g},\quad\gamma_g=\frac{\omega}{\omega_0}.\]

“This is a consistency calculation using the retained energy/inertia identification; no signalling limit is inserted to obtain it.” The last identity of FC08 “checks the internal phase along a monochromatic moving ray against D2's proper clock”. Symbolic checks 2 and 3, “low_momentum_inertial_matching” (whose positive solution is \(v=c\)) and “ray_phase_and_proper_clock”, pass (§20).

Further uses. A body's inertia includes its changing stored energy, \(m_j=\mathcal R_j/c^2\) (FC26), with the exact moving-body roots FC37 and FC46 (symbolic check 10).

Domain. Free internal modes at low momentum for the matching; bodies whose stored energy changes for FC26.

FCE-A03 · The rotation lift (for FCE-P03)

\[\frac{d\mathcal M_{\mathrm{enc}}}{dT}\lt0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\frac{d\Phi_g}{dT}\lt0 .\]

FCE-A18 · D4's conservation laws and work law (for FCE-P18)

Premise FCE-P18 · root physical premise, adopted as inputs in §11 · used for FCE-O15–FCE-O18

\[\frac{dE_{\mathrm{enc}}^{(A)}}{dt}=0,\qquad \frac{d\mathbf P}{dt}=0,\qquad dK=\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r=-\,dU .\]

Statement. “Draw a closed surface around a system and let nothing cross it. The complete energy inside, counted once in one observer's units, does not change”; the two laws “are stated for a closed system: no matter and no energy crosses its boundary”; “When only the energy of motion and a potential energy trade, the work done is the potential energy released” (D4, “What We Used to Derive the Physics”). This document adopts them as inputs.

Use here. FC01 writes the energy balance of a fixed enclosure with its boundary current; FC02 is the momentum balance of the bodies; FC58 applies energy conservation and the work law body by body, \(\dot K_i=\mathbf F_i\cdot\dot{\mathbf x}_i\); the circular trial applies energy and angular-momentum conservation with no other entry (§11). In the carrier model these balances are not assumed: they are proved for its Hamiltonian, exactly, during flight (FC29–FC32) and through both events (FC45–FC51).

FCE-A19 · Newton's law far away (for FCE-P19)

Premise FCE-P19 · empirical datum, inherited from D4 · used for FCE-O16

\[K=\frac{Gm_1m_2}{d^2}.\]

Source and method. D4: “Two constants are measured: \(G\), through Newton's law of gravitation far from a mass, and \(c\)” (“What We Used to Derive the Physics”). This document states no uncertainty for it; it is an inherited report, used here as D4 uses it.

Use here. The still body's inverse-square pull on each half and the scale \(K\) of the split; the probe is placed where “Newton's far law and the same local-response assumptions apply between it and every part” (§11).

FCE-A20 · The conditions of the energy balance for bodies that move (for FCE-P20)

Premise FCE-P20 · preparation and boundary condition: the stated conditions of FC58 · used for FCE-O18

FC58
\[0=(\mathbf F+\nabla_0 U)\cdot v_0+\sum_{j=1}^{m}\nabla_j U\cdot v_j .\]

Specification. The complete energy, apart from constant rest energy, is \(E=\sum_iK_i+U(q_0,q_1,\ldots,q_m)\), with \(q_0=q(T)\), \(q_j=q(T-\tau_j)\) at distinct positive lags and \(U\) differentiable and counted once; the sampled rates can vary independently with all sampled positions held fixed; in the velocity-dependent branch the force is finite at \(v_0=0\), with the earlier rates still independently variable there. Result under these conditions: a position-only pull is \(\mathbf F=-\nabla U(q_0)\) with \(U=U(q_0)\) locally, and a velocity-dependent remainder finite at zero present velocity has zero summed power.

What each condition is needed for: the document's derivation (§11)

Write \(v_j=dq_j/dT\) and collect the forces into \(\mathbf F\), so that \(\mathbf F\cdot v_0=\sum_i\mathbf F_i\cdot\dot{\mathbf x}_i\). The work law, energy conservation and the chain rule give FC58; this needs the complete energy in the stated form, with \(U\) differentiable and counted once.

Position-only pull. With the sampled positions fixed, “vary one earlier rate \(v_j\) at a time. The force stays fixed, so FC58 gives \(\nabla_jU=0\) for every \(j>0\). Thus \(U=U(q_0)\) locally. Now vary the present rate \(v_0\) in each direction. FC58 gives \(\mathbf F=-\nabla U(q_0)\). This fixes the whole position-only pull, including at a configuration where its power happens to vanish.” This needs the independent variations.

Varying lags. If a lag varies, its rate in FC58 is

\[v_j=(1-\dot\tau_j)\dot q(T-\tau_j),\]

and “The same argument applies wherever these actual sampled rates admit the stated independent variations.”

Velocity-dependent pull. “Take \(v_0=0\), with the force finite there and the earlier rates still independently variable. The present-force term in FC58 vanishes. Varying each earlier rate again gives \(\nabla_jU=0\) for every \(j>0\).” This needs the force to be finite at zero present velocity. At general \(v_0\),

\[\bigl(\mathbf F+\nabla U(q_0)\bigr)\cdot v_0=0,\]

so the remainder \(\mathbf R=\mathbf F+\nabla U(q_0)\) has zero summed instantaneous power, \(\sum_i\mathbf R_i\cdot\dot{\mathbf x}_i=0\); its powers on individual bodies may be nonzero. If the stored energy also depends on \(v_0\), its derivative contributes the additional term \((\partial U/\partial v_0)\cdot\dot v_0\) to the balance.

FCE-A21 · The no-emission split (for FCE-P21)

Premise FCE-P21 · preparation and boundary condition · used for FCE-O16

\[\sum_{\rm halves}F_{\rm axis}=-Kq,\qquad K=\frac{Gm_1m_2}{d^2},\qquad q=\Bigl(1+\frac{s^2}{d^2}\Bigr)^{-3/2}.\]

Specification. Body \(m_1\) is at rest at the origin; body \(m_2\), initially at distance \(d\), separates into halves at \((d,\pm s)\); no light is emitted. The halves' internal forces cancel. The still body's pull acts at each half's present place on its whole responding count \(m_2/2\). A probe is negligible and still, with Newton's far law and the same local-response assumptions between it and every part.

Support and consequences. With these specifications the summed force on the halves along the axis from \(m_1\) to the unsplit \(m_2\) is \(-Kq\), and FC02, with all momentum in the bodies, requires \(+Kq\) on the still body at the same \(T\). “This force evaluation is exact at the stated positions and holds to first order in the pulls for free motion” (§11).

FCE-A22 · The late trial law (for FCE-P22)

Premise FCE-P22 · comparison-only assumption: tested, not adopted · used for FCE-O17

\[\dot E=2vQ\sin\delta,\qquad \dot L=2aQ\sin\delta,\qquad \delta=(v/c)\cos\delta.\]

Content. Two equal bodies at opposite ends of a diameter on a circle of radius \(a\) each move at speed \(v\) and feel a pull of magnitude \(Q\) toward where the other was one light-travel time earlier. Here \(Q\) is the magnitude of that pull, as the trial states it.

Consequence. The trial law gives the displayed energy and angular-momentum rates. “With no other energy or angular-momentum entry, conservation excludes that late law in this configuration” (§11). The law is the comparison under test; no result of this document rests on it.

FCE-A23 · The particle criterion (for FCE-P23)

Premise FCE-P23 · definition · used for FCE-O02–FCE-O04, FCE-O08–FCE-O10

FC17
\[E_c\geq\sqrt{(Q\omega_0)^2+c^2P_c^2}.\]

Definition. “Here a model particle means a complete elementary admitted excitation with finite localized energy, autonomous motion between events, definite total translation momentum and internal spin, and a calculated physical creation/absorption process that transfers its charges” (§13). It is a definition of what the construction must exhibit, not a law.

Where each item is met

Complete elementary admitted excitation: \(Q=s_*\) (FC14). Finite localized energy: FC17 and the free energy density, with about 99.9662% of it within \(12\,\ell_0\) of its centre at birth and 99.7324% just before capture (§17). Autonomous motion between events: the free evolution of FC16 and the coupled evolution FC27. Definite total translation momentum and internal spin: FC10, FC18. Calculated creation and absorption that transfers its charges: FC35, FC44, FC48–FC50. “A packet may disperse while preserving its action and energy; the worked localization is measured in §17. No soliton or universal lifetime is presumed” (§13).

FCE-A24 · D5's force target (for FCE-P24)

Premise FCE-P24 · definition, imported from D5 · used for FCE-O05

\[\dot P_R=F_R=\varepsilon\,b^\dagger\mathcal E'(X_R)\,b.\]

Definition. D5 “Defines the construction target: a specified overlap domain, pairing, measure and calculated change in momentum” (§9). D5 is unpublished and enters only through this definition.

Construction here. Domain: the receiver window \(w(x-X)\) (FC22). Pairing and measure: “The common flat comparison frame supplies the pairing; dx/L and dμ are the measures” (§14). Calculated change in momentum: \(\dot P_R=F_R\) (FC27), with the opposite change of the carrier's momentum (FC30). Units: frequency for the matrix, energy for its contraction and force for its position derivative (§14).

FCE-A25 · D3's complete correlated states (for FCE-P25)

Premise FCE-P25 · imported definitions, subordinate to G1 and C1 · used for FCE-O13

FC57
\[\mathcal{C}_{T,\lambda}^{(a)}:X^-\longmapsto X^+,\qquad \lambda\in\Lambda_a(X^-).\]

Definitions. “Actualization, records, later responses and complete correlated states; the G1/C1 definitions govern” (§9). D3 is unpublished and enters only through these definitions.

Use here. “Let X denote the complete joint state: all sector coefficients, phases, centres and momenta, overlap terms, buffers, histories and records.” “The support set must preserve zero-weight forbidden outcomes in the complete correlated state, and every actual recoil or energy transfer must be included in X+.” “For two events at the same common T, commuting complete maps can be composed in either order. Otherwise the model must specify a joint map or an explicit physical order” (§19).

FCE-A26 · The prepared source and receiver (for FCE-P26)

Premise FCE-P26 · preparation and boundary condition · used for FCE-O04, FCE-O08, FCE-O09, FCE-O12

FC33
\[H_E^-=\mathcal{R}_E^-=M_{{\rm bare},E}c^2+B_E+E_{r,E}+(1-\kappa_E)\omega_0Q.\]

Specification. “The emitter begins at rest with one bound excitation \(a_E^\dagger a_E=Q=s_*\), an empty carrier field, and a ready record. An isotropic source overlap \(-\kappa_E\omega_0Q\), with \(0\lt\kappa_E\lt1\), gives” FC33, “the constant-weight specialization of the source's energy-overlap idea” (§15). The aperture is normalized, \(\sum_n|\alpha_n|^2=1\) (FC15), the packet is born as FC16, and the polarization is common, \(b_n=\beta_nu\) (§13). The receiver is at rest with a ready record and an empty bound slot. In the control trial “there is no prepared source excitation and b = 0” (§18).

Support. FC34–FC38 show that the source triggers at \(T_E=4\tau_0\) inside its capacity domain. “The source position, spectrum and inherited phase determine the packet. Its energy and momentum follow from the sums in FC10” (§13). The control is an exact solution with \(W_R=F_R=A_R=0\) (§18).

FCE-A27 · The flat, collinear, periodic laboratory (for FCE-P27)

Premise FCE-P27 · preparation and boundary condition · used for FCE-O01, FCE-O11, FCE-O12

FC22
\[w(y)=\frac{1}{Z_w}\sum_{r\in\mathbb{Z}}e^{-(y-rL)^2/(2a_w^2)},\qquad Z_w=\sum_{r\in\mathbb{Z}}e^{-(rL)^2/(2a_w^2)}.\]

Specification. The worked configuration is collinear, in a flat local laboratory with negligible gravitational self-interaction, with the internal spin polarization fixed during spatial coupling; periodicity is a flat translation-channel idealization, and the interaction ends well before the packet wraps around the period (§10). “The worked laboratory uses its flat local limit” of D4's rule (§18).

Support. “All centre motion is collinear, so the orbital angular momentum is zero and the complete angular momentum is the unchanged spin” (§17). “Both the finite Fourier packet and the periodized Gaussian window have global support. Consequently the chosen geometry does not impose a strict silent interval at the receiver” (§18).

FCE-A28 · The worked constants (for FCE-P28)

Premise FCE-P28 · preparation: the numerical inputs · used for FCE-O11

FC54
\[T_A-T_E=41.90159120135437\tau_0,\qquad T_A=45.90159120135437\tau_0.\]

Specification. The values of the register entry FCE-P28, from the input table of §17; the calculation sets \(s_*=\omega_0=c=1\) and \(T_0=0\).

Support. The capacities are bounded over the whole refined band before the packet is chosen: “A bound over the entire refined band, rather than only the selected Gaussian, gives Ec ≤ 3.9002859303E₀ and |Pc| ≤ 3.7699111843p₀ at Q = s*” (§17). The trajectory's residuals and the N = 96 refinement are in §20; the scripts that reproduce every value are embedded there.

08 / Summaries

The seven sections for a child, a physics teacher and a theoretical physicist

For a child

Imagine a tiny ripple that one toy can throw and another toy can catch. The ripple carries a little push and a little spin. What we asked (section 1): can such a ripple be thrown, pull on the catcher on its way, and be caught, with every bit of energy, push and spin counted, nothing lost and nothing made from nothing? How (section 2): we wrote down the ripple's rules and worked out how it moves. The thrower lets the ripple go when its counter reaches one whole unit; the catcher catches it when its own counter reaches one whole unit; in between, the ripple tugs on the catcher, and we followed every tug. What we started from (sections 3 to 5): we listed every starting point, said which come from other papers and which are new here, and for each one showed where it comes from and what we checked. Where each result comes from (section 6): every result has its steps and its checks. The tests (section 7): they all pass. At every moment the energy, the push and the spin add up to the same totals.

We also checked a rule from the gravity paper: clocks and rulers everywhere change at once, and light does not carry the change. Counting energy and push shows what goes wrong otherwise. A thing that kept sending out light to keep its pull could not keep its pull the same. If a pull waited for light, the pushes on two bodies would not balance. And two bodies going round a circle, each pulled toward where the other used to be, would gain energy from nothing. So, in these tests, the pull points to where things are now.

For a physics teacher

Scope (1). The page builds one carrier of a force from an internal wave already used for spin: a wavepacket that a source emits, that pulls on a receiver through an energy overlap, and that the receiver absorbs, with energy, momentum, action and spin conserved exactly at every point. It also asks what the two conservation arguments behind the gravity paper's premise 6 establish. Method (2). The wave equation gives \(\omega^2=\omega_0^2+c^2k^2\), with the speed \(c\) fixed by matching the packet's inertia to its energy, \(m=Q\omega_0/c^2\), and no signalling limit assumed. The packet's action is one admitted unit, \(Q=s_*\), which the calibration CAL identifies with \(\hbar\). The receiver couples through \(U_R=-\varepsilon\times\)(the overlap of its window with the packet's energy), and the force on the receiver follows from how that overlap changes with the receiver's position. Emission and absorption are complete events at action thresholds, with exact recoil and internal-energy accounting. In the worked example the receiver records the packet at \(T_A=45.9015912014\,\tau_0\) and ends with momentum \(+1\,p_0\). Premises, dependencies and appendices (3–5). Twenty-eight inputs are listed with their status: imported results from the spin, granularity and collapse papers, the gravity paper's premises 1, 3, 5 and 6 and its conservation laws, new completions made here, definitions, preparations, one calibration, one measured law and one tested trial law; each has an appendix. Traceability and tests (6–7). Every result is linked to its derivation and checks: fifteen exact identities pass, and the numerical residuals are below \(10^{-12}\). The update at once. Continual outward light cannot keep an unpowered source's pull unchanged. When a body splits without emitting light, momentum conservation requires the still body to feel the present-configuration pull \(+Kq\) at the same moment, exactly at the stated positions and to first order in the pulls for free motion, and any late or partial response leaves momentum unbalanced by the amount of its departure. A late pull on two bodies in a circle gains energy and angular momentum from nothing. For moving bodies whose complete energy is their kinetic energy plus one potential of finitely many sampled configurations, with independently variable sampled rates, energy conservation requires a position-only pull to be minus the gradient of a present-configuration potential.

For a theoretical physicist

Scope and method (1–2). The action FC05 on a flat periodic channel times \(K=SU(2)\) gives FC06–FC08; matching the low-momentum inertia to D2's G2 fixes \(v=c\). The canonical charges FC10 are conserved in free motion, and G1's tensor on the enlarged finite family admits \(Q=N_Qs_*\) (FC13–FC14). The receiver couples through \(U_R=-\varepsilon b^\dagger\mathcal E(X_R)b\), with \(0\le\mathcal E\le\mathsf D\) and \(H_c\geq(1-\varepsilon)E_c>0\) for every retained finite family (FC25); translation covariance gives the exact identities FC29–FC32. Emission and capture are FC-TRANSFER events on one common \(T\) slice, with exact moving-body roots FC37 and FC46 inside the capacity domains FC38 and FC47, and a phase-anchored capture of weight one. 11 / Exact audit of the instantaneous-update argument

Keep the adopted law and state what conservation establishes

Uses: FCE-P14–FCE-P22. Fulfils: FCE-O14–FCE-O18. Derivation: FC01–FC04 and FC58; traceability rows FCE-R14–FCE-R18; appendices FCE-A15–FCE-A22. Domain: D4's inventory: an unpowered steady source between two Gaussian surfaces; the no-emission split, exact at the stated positions and to first order in the pulls for free motion; two equal bodies on a circle; bodies that move, under the stated energy and history conditions.

D4 §3 premise 6 gives two arguments for instantaneous ruler updates. The first concerns continual outward energy expenditure; the second starts from a complete body-momentum inventory. What each establishes, and where the further inference to present places holds, can be stated precisely.

Continuing outward expenditure

For a fixed enclosure, complete energy accounting gives

FC01

An unpowered source with continuing positive net outward energy current loses enclosed energy and, under D4's flux/count rule, its pull decreases. Continual net outward light therefore cannot maintain the time-invariant gravitational force that D4 premise 1 gives between the two Gaussian surfaces when nothing crosses the source's surface. D4 premise 6 calls this failure of the proposed upkeep ‘against premise 1’. The depletion itself satisfies (FC01). The further assertion that every finite-speed change must require perpetual outward expenditure does not follow from this equation. In this construction, a source releases a finite excitation and a larger closed inventory retains its energy throughout the transfer. The excitation carries energy to the receiver. The construction keeps D4's clock-and-ruler update at once on the common \(T\) slice (§18).

For two equal bodies at opposite ends of a diameter on a circle of radius \(a\), let each move at speed \(v\) and feel a pull of magnitude \(Q\) toward where the other was one light-travel time earlier. This gives \(\dot E=2vQ\sin\delta\) and \(\dot L=2aQ\sin\delta\), with \(\delta=(v/c)\cos\delta\). With no other energy or angular-momentum entry, conservation excludes that late law in this configuration.

Momentum balance and present positions

The source writes

FC02

For exactly two bodies and no omitted momentum, this gives equal and opposite forces at a common time. It does not determine a force's dependence on present positions, previous data or an additional dynamical state. Even a direction along the separation would require an appropriate angular-momentum condition as well. D4 §4 statement 8 supplies the separate current-configuration rule

FC03

FC03 is retained as the author's instantaneous premise. FC02 alone does not derive its particular time dependence.

In the no-emission split, body \(m_1\) is at rest at the origin and body \(m_2\), initially at distance \(d\), separates into halves at \((d,\pm s)\). The still body's inverse-square pull acts at each half's present place on its whole responding count, \(m_2/2\) (D4 premise 5). The halves' internal forces cancel, and their summed force along the axis from \(m_1\) to the unsplit \(m_2\) is \(-Kq\), where \(K=Gm_1m_2/d^2\) and \(q=(1+s^2/d^2)^{-3/2}\). With all momentum in the bodies (D4 premise 6), FC02 requires \(+Kq\) on the still body at that same \(T\). Every departure from \(+Kq\), including a partial or late response, leaves momentum unbalanced by the amount of the departure. This force evaluation is exact at the stated positions and holds to first order in the pulls for free motion. To that order the result holds at each placement of a negligible still probe where Newton's far law and the same local-response assumptions apply between it and every part. With D4's clock step applied on each \(T\) slice and the clock rate normalized to one at infinity, the rates of clocks held at rest there follow at once, to the same order.

Energy balance for bodies that move. Collect the positions of the bodies into \(q\). Write \(q_0=q(T)\) for their present configuration and \(q_j=q(T-\tau_j)\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\), for finitely many earlier configurations at distinct positive lags. Suppose the complete energy, apart from constant rest energy, is

\[E=\sum_i K_i+U(q_0,q_1,\ldots,q_m),\]

where \(U\) is differentiable and counted once. Write \(v_j=dq_j/dT\) for the rate of each sampled configuration and collect the forces on the bodies into \(\mathbf F\). Then \(\mathbf F\cdot v_0=\sum_i\mathbf F_i\cdot\dot{\mathbf x}_i\). By the work law \(\dot K_i=\mathbf F_i\cdot\dot{\mathbf x}_i\), energy conservation and the chain rule give

FC58
\[0=(\mathbf F+\nabla_0 U)\cdot v_0+\sum_{j=1}^{m}\nabla_j U\cdot v_j .\]

Suppose the sampled rates can vary independently while all the sampled positions are held fixed. For a pull that depends only on those positions, vary one earlier rate \(v_j\) at a time. The force stays fixed, so FC58 gives \(\nabla_jU=0\) for every \(j>0\). Thus \(U=U(q_0)\) locally. Now vary the present rate \(v_0\) in each direction. FC58 gives \(\mathbf F=-\nabla U(q_0)\). This fixes the whole position-only pull, including at a configuration where its power happens to vanish.

For fixed lags the earlier rates are \(v_j=\dot q(T-\tau_j)\). If a lag varies, its rate in FC58 is

\[v_j=(1-\dot\tau_j)\dot q(T-\tau_j).\]

The same argument applies wherever these actual sampled rates admit the stated independent variations.

For a velocity-dependent pull with the same positional energy, take \(v_0=0\), with the force finite there and the earlier rates still independently variable. The present-force term in FC58 vanishes. Varying each earlier rate again gives \(\nabla_jU=0\) for every \(j>0\). At general \(v_0\) the remaining equation is

\[\bigl(\mathbf F+\nabla U(q_0)\bigr)\cdot v_0=0.\]

Thus the remainder \(\mathbf R=\mathbf F+\nabla U(q_0)\) has zero summed instantaneous power, \(\sum_i\mathbf R_i\cdot\dot{\mathbf x}_i=0\). Its powers on individual bodies may be nonzero. If the stored energy itself also depends on \(v_0\), its derivative contributes the additional term \((\partial U/\partial v_0)\cdot\dot v_0\) to the balance.

D4 §6 already distinguishes a geometric change from registration by an instrument and leaves the response calculation to be supplied. Section 18 supplies that response for this carrier's chosen detector.

The carrier must enter the complete inventory

FC04

The new packet counts as a physical excitation in this inventory. Clocks and rulers still carry no separate momentum. During flight the original source and receiver alone can have a changing total momentum because the carrier holds the remainder. Requiring their pair alone to remain balanced would discard the very quantity the proposed carrier transports.

The moving two-body energy statement in D4 §4 is explicitly a first-order result; it is not used here as an exact general many-body Hamiltonian. This construction supplies its own complete flat-laboratory Hamiltonian below. The selected carrier overlap is counted once as UR. It is not also charged as another copy of the background gravitational interaction.

18 / Equal-time geometry, collapse, transport and registration

Calculate the temporal claims separately

Uses: FCE-P07, FCE-P13, FCE-P15, FCE-P26, FCE-P27. Fulfils: FCE-O12. Derivation: the table and the record protocol of this section; traceability row FCE-R12. Domain: the common T slice in the flat local laboratory.

ObjectSpecified action in this constructionCalculated consequence
Equal-time background geometryD4's current-configuration clock/ruler rule is retained. The worked laboratory uses its flat local limit.No extra geometry momentum or duplicated gravitational potential enters this carrier ledger.
Complete collapse eventEmission creates the whole prepared field at TE; absorption removes the whole field and resets the complete receiving apparatus at TA.Each event acts at a single common T over the complete configuration and conserves its total charges.
Independent carrierBetween those events, FC27 evolves the field and receiver. The free limit has dispersion FC08 and energy current FC12.The packet has a calculated moving energy concentration, changing overlap and mechanical force.
Readable terminal recordThe receiver writes + at its first supported overlap-action threshold.Its computed record time is TA = 45.9015912014τ₀, not the emission time.

Both the finite Fourier packet and the periodized Gaussian window have global support. Consequently the chosen geometry does not impose a strict silent interval at the receiver. Immediately after emission its overlap is already WR = 7.24022 × 10−9E₀ and its force is −7.97751 × 10−9E₀/ℓ₀. That is an immediate state-dependent force change in the model. The finite registration time is set by the actual threshold law, not by declaring those tails absent.

A specified record protocol

Take two independently prepared trials with the same ready receiver. In trial 1 the source contains and emits the specified excitation. In trial 0 there is no prepared source excitation and b = 0. The latter is an exact solution: WR = FR = AR = 0, and its record remains ready. Reading the receiver at the calculated TA therefore distinguishes written + from ready and implements one ideal prepared binary channel.

The preparation distinguishes the two physical inputs; no uncounted source-switching work is assigned at a later time. This is an explicit terminal-record protocol without a noise or instrument-resolution model. The nonzero immediate force is calculated, but a separate continuously monitored force-readout apparatus has not been introduced. Thus the specified record channel is completed at TA; its calculation does not equate an instantaneous configuration change with an instantaneously completed message.

The common-time event hypothesis is implemented exactly as selected. The finite-band dynamics and global event support determine the temporal behavior above; a monochromatic group velocity alone is not a signal-front theorem. No conventional light-cone restriction has been imposed to replace D4's time structure.

19 / Internal spin and the reserved sector interface

Retain the internal geometry throughout the transfer

Uses: FCE-P03, FCE-P07, FCE-P25. Fulfils: FCE-O13. Derivation: FC56–FC57; traceability row FCE-R13. Domain: the polarized branch and the complete joint state.

Every bn belongs to D2's same lowest internal doublet. A spatially uniform internal physical rotation therefore acts with the inherited lift

FC56

The energy overlap is identity on that doublet. Rotation thus commutes with the spatial evolution and the complete common-polarization transfer law, while the spin rotates as the corresponding vector. The retained 2π sign and 4π return belong to the complete coefficients and remain available in coherent comparisons. Under CAL, the elementary carrier has the already-derived internal spin magnitude ℏ/2 in this polarized branch. The number of detector channels was not used to assign it.

The selected flat comparison frame requires no new transport component. Rest/internal energies enter the source and receiver masses by FC26, and the pure-mode moving phase satisfies FC08. These are the interfaces needed by the present event. The full spin/curvature reconciliation remains a separate task (the reconciliation of granularity, collapse, spin and curvature).

Reserve individual-sector collapse without assuming decay

Let X denote the complete joint state: all sector coefficients, phases, centres and momenta, overlap terms, buffers, histories and records. A later event associated with sector a can be denoted

FC57

The label a specifies where the transition is initiated; it does not authorize independent marginal selection. The support set must preserve zero-weight forbidden outcomes in the complete correlated state, and every actual recoil or energy transfer must be included in X+. For two events at the same common T, commuting complete maps can be composed in either order. Otherwise the model must specify a joint map or an explicit physical order; changing order cannot be hidden by notation.

This construction supplies the transfer and accounting interface for such a map. It supplies no decay products, decay rate or decay lifetime. “Separate internal-space collapse causes decay” remains the reserved hypothesis, not an extra result of this construction.

20 / Exact identities and bounded numerical verification

Verify the physical claims used by this construction

The conservation proofs FC29–32 and FC45–51 are analytic. A separate symbolic script checks 15 mathematical claims covering dispersion, inertial matching, proper phase, translation and spin symmetry, smooth conservation, free-current sign, physical event roots and oscillator resets. All 15 pass. These checks parametrize positive-buffer event states; the independent capacity bounds in §17 establish that the example belongs to that domain.

The trajectory uses DOP853 with relative tolerance 2 × 10−13, absolute tolerance 2 × 10−15 and maximum step 0.1τ₀. The active N = 80 run has 161 spatial modes. At 301 uniformly spaced samples over the full interaction, the largest absolute action, energy and momentum residuals are 5.44 × 10−13s*, 8.64 × 10−13E₀ and 6.55 × 10−13p₀. The final complete energy residual after both events is 9.10 × 10−13E₀ in magnitude.

A 193-mode N = 96 run changes the absorption time by 4.64 × 10−9τ₀ and the smooth receiver impulse by 7.47 × 10−11p₀. The final receiver buffer agrees at the displayed precision because its analytic endpoint follows from FC48. This bounded refinement supports the displayed packet trajectory; it is not a claim of exact compression of every continuum wave.

Independent physical-space quadrature of the canonical energy agrees with the Fourier matrix to 2.23 × 10−16E₀ for total free energy and 5.56 × 10−17E₀ for overlap energy. Twenty-four independent complex-state/translation samples verify covariance and the continuous conservation derivatives, and the two-mode nonzero force FC28 agrees directly. The oscillator coordinates reproduce their calculated final energies. The zero-field control remains an exact no-click state.

The complete scripts and results are embedded below. Saving each script as its shown filename in one folder reproduces its calculations. The trajectory script needs Python, NumPy, SciPy and threadpoolctl; the exact checks use SymPy. Their numerical arrays are a representation of the selected finite domain, not physical grains.

Reproducible trajectory, energy-overlap and event verification — verify_carrier.py
"""Reproduce the complete example and bounded verification.
Requires Python 3, numpy, scipy, threadpoolctl; writes results and plot data beside this file.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp
from threadpoolctl import threadpool_limits

ROOT=Path(__file__).parent

def run(N=80,rtol=2e-13,atol=2e-15,max_step=.1,dense=False):
    # Units: s*=omega0=c=1; length c/omega0, energy s*omega0.
    L=160.; Q=1.; c=1.; omega0=1.
    n=np.arange(-N,N+1);k=2*np.pi*n/L;om=np.sqrt(omega0**2+c*c*k*k)
    M=2*N+1; eps=.1; sig_w=4.;sig_k=.15;k0=1.;XE=-30.;XR=0.
    wnorm=L/(np.sqrt(2*np.pi)*sig_w)*sum(np.exp(-(.5*(j*L/sig_w)**2)) for j in range(-3,4))
    diff=k[None,:]-k[:,None]
    wh=np.exp(-.5*sig_w**2*diff**2)/wnorm
    energyfactor=(om[:,None]*om[None,:]+c*c*k[:,None]*k[None,:]+omega0**2)/(2*np.sqrt(om[:,None]*om[None,:]))
    Ebase=wh*energyfactor
    def Emat(X):return Ebase*np.exp(1j*diff*X)
    def quantities(b,X,P):
        E=Emat(X);Eb=E@b
        return dict(Q=float(np.vdot(b,b).real),Ec=float(np.vdot(b,om*b).real),Pc=float(np.vdot(b,k*b).real),W=float(eps*np.vdot(b,Eb).real),F=float(eps*np.vdot(b,(1j*diff*E)@b).real))
    alpha=np.exp(-.25*((k-k0)/sig_k)**2);alpha/=np.linalg.norm(alpha)
    kappaE=.25;TE=1/(kappaE*omega0)
    phaseE=np.exp(-1j*(1-kappaE)*omega0*TE)
    b0=np.sqrt(Q)*phaseE*alpha*np.exp(-1j*k*XE)
    bareE=bareR=1000.;BE=BR=10.;ERE=ERR=.2;boundomega=1.
    restR=bareR+BR+ERR
    q0=quantities(b0,XR,0.)
    Hsrc0=bareE+BE+ERE+(1-kappaE)*omega0*Q
    Hrec0=restR
    F0=q0['Ec']-q0['W'];Psrc=-q0['Pc'];Hsrc=Hsrc0-F0
    restsrc=np.sqrt(Hsrc**2-c*c*Psrc**2);BEafter=restsrc-bareE
    Epair=Hrec0+F0;Ppair=q0['Pc']
    y0=np.r_[b0.real,b0.imag,XR,0.,0.]
    def unpack(y):return y[:M]+1j*y[M:2*M],float(y[-3]),float(y[-2]),float(y[-1])
    def rhs(t,y):
        b,X,P,A=unpack(y);E=Emat(X);Eb=E@b
        db=-1j*(om*b-eps*Eb)
        force=eps*np.vdot(b,(1j*diff*E)@b).real
        W=eps*np.vdot(b,Eb).real
        return np.r_[db.real,db.imag,c*c*P/np.sqrt(restR**2+c*c*P*P),force,W]
    def trigger(t,y):return y[-1]-Q
    trigger.direction=1;trigger.terminal=True
    sol=solve_ivp(rhs,(0,100),y0,method='DOP853',rtol=rtol,atol=atol,max_step=max_step,events=trigger,dense_output=True)
    assert sol.success and len(sol.t_events[0])==1,sol.message
    TA=float(sol.t_events[0][0]);b,X,P,A=unpack(sol.y_events[0][0]);qa=quantities(b,X,P)
    Hrec=np.sqrt(restR**2+P*P)
    Hrecafter=Hrec+qa['Ec']-qa['W'];Precafter=P+qa['Pc']
    restrecafter=np.sqrt(Hrecafter**2-Precafter**2);BRafter=restrecafter-bareR-boundomega*Q
    beta_anchor=alpha*np.exp(-1j*k*X)
    anchor=np.vdot(beta_anchor,b)
    aR=np.sqrt(Q)*anchor/abs(anchor)
    # Uniform time samples check conservation over the entire flight.
    times=np.linspace(0,TA,301);ys=sol.sol(times)
    errors={'Q':0.,'energy':0.,'momentum':0.}
    samples=[]
    for t,y in zip(times,ys.T):
        bt,xt,pt,at=unpack(y);q=quantities(bt,xt,pt)
        ht=np.sqrt(restR**2+pt*pt)
        errors['Q']=max(errors['Q'],abs(q['Q']-Q))
        errors['energy']=max(errors['energy'],abs((ht-restR)+q['Ec']-q['W']-F0))
        errors['momentum']=max(errors['momentum'],abs(pt+q['Pc']-Ppair))
        samples.append([float(t),xt,pt,at,q['Ec'],q['Pc'],q['W'],q['F']])
    result={'N':N,'mode_count':M,'rtol':rtol,'atol':atol,'max_step':max_step,'steps':len(sol.t),'evaluations':sol.nfev,'emission_time':TE,'flight_time':TA,'absolute_absorption_time':TE+TA,'initial':q0,'before_absorption':dict(qa,X=X,P=P,A=A,Hbody=Hrec),'source':{'H_before':Hsrc0,'H_after':Hsrc,'P_after':Psrc,'rest_after':restsrc,'buffer_after':BEafter},'receiver':{'H_before_emission':Hrec0,'H_after_absorption':Hrecafter,'P_after_absorption':Precafter,'rest_after_absorption':restrecafter,'buffer_after_absorption':BRafter},'initial_total':Hsrc0+Hrec0,'final_total':Hsrc+Hrecafter,'errors':errors,'phase_anchor_abs':float(abs(anchor)),'receiver_amplitude_real':float(aR.real),'receiver_amplitude_imag':float(aR.imag),'final_errors':{'energy':float(Hsrc+Hrecafter-Hsrc0-Hrec0),'momentum':float(Psrc+Precafter),'receiver_birth_invariant_energy':float(Hrecafter-Epair),'receiver_birth_invariant_momentum':float(Precafter-Ppair)},'wnorm':wnorm}
    if dense:
        np.savez(ROOT/'flight_data.npz',times=times,y=ys,k=k,omega=om,alpha=alpha,b0=b0,source_pos=XE+Psrc/Hsrc*times,samples=np.array(samples),Ebase=Ebase)
    return result

def verify_and_run():
    with threadpool_limits(limits=1):
        primary=run(N=80,dense=True)
        refinement=run(N=96)
    (ROOT/'flight_runs.json').write_text(json.dumps({'primary':primary,'refinement':refinement},indent=2))
    arr=np.load(ROOT/'flight_data.npz')
    k=arr['k'];om=arr['omega'];b0=arr['b0'];Ebase=arr['Ebase']
    times=arr['times'];ys=arr['y'];M=len(k)
    errors={}
    rng=np.random.default_rng(20261126)
    diff=k[None,:]-k[:,None]
    L=160.;a=4.;eps=.1
    def EM(X):return Ebase*np.exp(1j*diff*X)
    # An independent physical-space integral checks the energy-overlap coefficients.
    xx=np.linspace(-L/2,L/2,4096,endpoint=False)
    basis=np.exp(1j*np.outer(xx,k))
    beta=(rng.normal(size=M)+1j*rng.normal(size=M));beta/=np.linalg.norm(beta)
    Xtest=3.17
    za=sum(np.exp(-.5*(j*L/a)**2) for j in range(-3,4))
    w=sum(np.exp(-.5*((xx-Xtest+j*L)/a)**2) for j in range(-2,3))/za
    f=basis@(beta/np.sqrt(om))
    vv=basis@(-1j*np.sqrt(om)*beta)
    fx=basis@(1j*k*beta/np.sqrt(om))
    energy_density=.5*(abs(vv)**2+abs(fx)**2+abs(f)**2)
    errors['physical_space_free_energy']=float(abs(np.mean(energy_density)-np.vdot(beta,om*beta).real))
    errors['physical_space_overlap_energy']=float(abs(np.mean(w*energy_density)-np.vdot(beta,EM(Xtest)@beta).real))
    # Test exact frame translation and the derived conservation derivatives.
    maxima={name:0. for name in ['translation_energy','translation_force','Q_dot','momentum_dot','total_energy_dot','spin_dot']}
    min_energy=1e9;max_fraction=0.
    for _ in range(24):
        b=rng.normal(size=M)+1j*rng.normal(size=M);b/=np.linalg.norm(b)
        X=float(rng.uniform(-20,20));P=float(rng.uniform(-2,2));shift=float(rng.uniform(-10,10))
        E=EM(X);Ex=1j*diff*E;H=np.diag(om)-eps*E
        db=-1j*(H@b);F=float(eps*np.vdot(b,Ex@b).real)
        rest=1010.2;velocity=P/np.sqrt(rest**2+P*P)
        bc=np.exp(-1j*k*shift)*b;Ec=EM(X+shift);Ecx=1j*diff*Ec
        vals={
          'translation_energy':np.vdot(b,E@b)-np.vdot(bc,Ec@bc),
          'translation_force':np.vdot(b,Ex@b)-np.vdot(bc,Ecx@bc),
          'Q_dot':2*np.vdot(b,db).real,
          'momentum_dot':2*np.vdot(k*b,db).real+F,
          'total_energy_dot':2*np.vdot(H@b,db).real-eps*np.vdot(b,Ex@b).real*velocity+F*velocity,
          'spin_dot':np.sqrt(.25)*abs(2*np.vdot(b,db).real)
        }
        for name,val in vals.items():maxima[name]=max(maxima[name],float(abs(val)))
        free=float(np.vdot(b,om*b).real);over=float(np.vdot(b,E@b).real)
        min_energy=min(min_energy,free-eps*over);max_fraction=max(max_fraction,over/free)
        assert -1e-12<=over<=free+1e-12
    errors.update(maxima)
    for err in errors.values():assert err<2e-12,errors
    # A deliberately nonzero two-mode force checks the physical response sign.
    two=np.zeros(M,complex);j0=np.where(k==0)[0][0];j1=j0+8
    two[j0]=1/np.sqrt(2);two[j1]=1/np.sqrt(2)
    xt=2.3;et=EM(xt);actual=eps*np.vdot(two,(1j*diff*et)@two).real
    expected=-eps*(k[j1]-k[j0])*Ebase[j0,j1]*np.sin((k[j1]-k[j0])*xt)
    assert abs(actual-expected)<2e-14 and abs(actual)>1e-4
    # Capacity follows before choosing the packet, using the entire refined band.
    kmax=2*np.pi*96/L;emax=np.sqrt(1+kmax*kmax)
    source_buffer_lower=np.sqrt((1010.95-emax)**2-kmax*kmax)-1000
    receiver_buffer_lower=np.sqrt((1010.2+.9)**2-kmax*kmax)-1001
    assert source_buffer_lower>0 and receiver_buffer_lower>0
    # Integrate the receiver's physical oscillator clock from its actual trajectory.
    from scipy.integrate import simpson
    Pvals=arr['samples'][:,2];proper=simpson(1010.2/np.sqrt(1010.2**2+Pvals**2),x=times)
    source=primary['source'];receiver=primary['receiver']
    phaseE0=.2;phaseR0=.4;nu=.7;mass_b=1.
    phaseE_birth=phaseE0+nu*primary['emission_time']
    phaseE_end=phaseE_birth+nu*source['rest_after']/source['H_after']*primary['flight_time']
    phaseR_end=phaseR0+nu*(primary['emission_time']+proper)
    qE=np.sqrt(2*source['buffer_after']/(mass_b*nu**2))*np.sin(phaseE_end)
    pE=np.sqrt(2*mass_b*source['buffer_after'])*np.cos(phaseE_end)
    qR=np.sqrt(2*receiver['buffer_after_absorption']/(mass_b*nu**2))*np.sin(phaseR_end)
    pR=np.sqrt(2*mass_b*receiver['buffer_after_absorption'])*np.cos(phaseR_end)
    realizedE=pE*pE/(2*mass_b)+mass_b*nu*nu*qE*qE/2
    realizedR=pR*pR/(2*mass_b)+mass_b*nu*nu*qR*qR/2
    assert abs(realizedE-source['buffer_after'])<1e-13
    assert abs(realizedR-receiver['buffer_after_absorption'])<1e-13
    resolution={
      'flight_time_difference':abs(primary['flight_time']-refinement['flight_time']),
      'initial_free_energy_difference':abs(primary['initial']['Ec']-refinement['initial']['Ec']),
      'smooth_receiver_impulse_difference':abs(primary['before_absorption']['P']-refinement['before_absorption']['P']),
      'receiver_buffer_difference':abs(primary['receiver']['buffer_after_absorption']-refinement['receiver']['buffer_after_absorption'])
    }
    assert max(resolution.values())<1e-7,resolution
    assert max(primary['errors'].values())<3e-11,primary['errors']
    assert primary['phase_anchor_abs']>.1
    assert min(source['buffer_after'],receiver['buffer_after_absorption'])>0
    # Envelope localization: normalized canonical action at birth and immediately before capture.
    bf=ys[:M,-1]+1j*ys[M:2*M,-1]
    profiles=[]
    for label,b in [('birth',b0),('pre_capture',bf)]:
        Phi=basis@b;rho=abs(Phi)**2/L
        centre=float(np.sum(xx*rho)*(L/len(xx))/np.sum(rho*(L/len(xx))))
        variance=float(np.sum((xx-centre)**2*rho)*(L/len(xx))/np.sum(rho*(L/len(xx))))
        fraction12=float(np.sum(rho[abs(xx-centre)<=12])*(L/len(xx))/np.sum(rho*(L/len(xx))))
        f=basis@(b/np.sqrt(om));vv=basis@(-1j*np.sqrt(om)*b);fx=basis@(1j*k*b/np.sqrt(om))
        e=.5*(abs(vv)**2+abs(fx)**2+abs(f)**2)/L
        energy_centre=float(np.sum(xx*e)/np.sum(e))
        energy_width=float(np.sqrt(np.sum((xx-energy_centre)**2*e)/np.sum(e)))
        energy_fraction12=float(np.sum(e[abs(xx-energy_centre)<=12])/np.sum(e))
        profiles.append({'label':label,'mean_x':centre,'rms_width':np.sqrt(variance),'action_fraction_within_12_of_mean':fraction12,
                         'free_energy_mean_x':energy_centre,'free_energy_rms_width':energy_width,'free_energy_fraction_within_12_of_mean':energy_fraction12})
    mean_v=float(np.vdot(b0,(k/om)*b0).real)
    invariant_gap=primary['initial']['Ec']**2-primary['initial']['Pc']**2-1
    result={'construction':'force-carrying excitation','status':'PASS','primary':primary,'resolution_run':refinement,'resolution_differences':resolution,
      'independent_checks':errors,'translation_and_derivative_sample_count':24,
      'two_mode_force':{'computed':float(actual),'analytic':float(expected)},
      'capacity_bounds_for_refined_band':{'kmax':kmax,'free_energy_upper':emax,'source_buffer_lower':float(source_buffer_lower),'receiver_buffer_lower':float(receiver_buffer_lower)},
      'realized_buffers':{'source_q_at_capture_time':float(qE),'source_p_at_capture_time':float(pE),'receiver_q_after_capture':float(qR),'receiver_p_after_capture':float(pR),'source_energy':float(realizedE),'receiver_energy':float(realizedR),'receiver_flight_proper_time':float(proper)},
      'localized_envelopes':profiles,'initial_mean_free_group_velocity':mean_v,'initial_free_energy_centroid_velocity':primary['initial']['Pc']/primary['initial']['Ec'],'packet_invariant_energy_excess_squared':invariant_gap,
      'no_emission_control':{'carrier_Q':0,'carrier_P':0,'receiver_force':0,'receiver_exposure':0,'receiver_click':False},
      'scope':['All energies include canonical temporal, spatial-gradient and internal-gradient terms.',
               'The finite-band Hamiltonian and event accounting are exact mathematical definitions; the displayed trajectory is numerical.',
               'The single phase-anchored capture channel is an explicitly adopted complete event, not a Born rule inferred from overlap.',
               'Positive-frequency finite-band packets and periodized Gaussian windows have global tails.',
               'The group velocity and computed finite registration time are not a strict signal-front theorem.',
               'The complete body rest energy changes with internal excitation, oscillator and record energy.']}
    (ROOT/'verification_results.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
    print(json.dumps({k:result[k] for k in ['construction','status','resolution_differences','independent_checks','capacity_bounds_for_refined_band','localized_envelopes','packet_invariant_energy_excess_squared']},indent=2))
    print(json.dumps({'primary':primary},indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':
    verify_and_run()
Independent exact identities — verify_symbolic.py
"""Exact checks for the selected carrier branch.

Run with Python 3 and SymPy.  This script performs no trajectory integration.
Each reported check is one mathematical claim, even when its verification
uses several components.  The event checks parametrize the positive final
buffer domain; they do not certify a numerical trajectory's capacity.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import sympy as sp


CHECKS: list[dict] = []


def check(name: str, residuals, meaning: str) -> None:
    if not isinstance(residuals, (list, tuple)):
        residuals = [residuals]
    scalars = []
    for item in residuals:
        if isinstance(item, sp.MatrixBase):
            scalars.extend(list(item))
        else:
            scalars.append(item)
    failures = []
    for expression in scalars:
        residual = sp.simplify(sp.trigsimp(sp.expand(expression)))
        if residual != 0:
            failures.append(str(residual))
    CHECKS.append(
        {
            "name": name,
            "passed": not failures,
            "meaning": meaning,
            "nonzero_residuals": failures,
        }
    )


# Common positive scales; momenta and wavenumbers may have either sign.
c, v, w0, Q = sp.symbols("c v omega0 Q", positive=True)
p, k = sp.symbols("p k", real=True)
w = sp.sqrt(w0**2 + c**2 * k**2)
vg = sp.diff(w, k)
gamma = w / w0

# 1. The selected single-mode dispersion contains its internal rest energy.
check(
    "single_mode_dispersion_and_mass_shell",
    [(Q * w) ** 2 - c**2 * (Q * k) ** 2 - (Q * w0) ** 2],
    "E=Q omega and p=Q k obey E^2-c^2 p^2=(Q omega0)^2.",
)

# 2. Match an initially unspecified propagation coefficient to D2's inertia.
energy_general = Q * sp.sqrt(w0**2 + v**2 * (p / Q) ** 2)
inverse_inertia = sp.diff(energy_general, p, 2).subs(p, 0)
mass_kinetic = sp.simplify(1 / inverse_inertia)
mass_d2 = Q * w0 / c**2
positive_solutions = sp.solve(sp.Eq(mass_kinetic, mass_d2), v)
check(
    "low_momentum_inertial_matching",
    [
        energy_general.subs(p, 0) - Q * w0,
        mass_kinetic - Q * w0 / v**2,
        mass_kinetic.subs(v, c) - mass_d2,
        sp.Integer(0 if positive_solutions == [c] else 1),
    ],
    "The low-p inertial mass is Q omega0/v^2; positive v matching D2 is c.",
)

# 3. Phase sampled along the group ray advances at the proper-time rate.
check(
    "ray_phase_and_proper_clock",
    [
        w - k * vg - w0 / gamma,
        1 - vg**2 / c**2 - 1 / gamma**2,
    ],
    "omega-k v_g=omega0/gamma, with the same gamma fixed by v_g.",
)

# General Hermitian two-mode comparison: enough to check the commutator signs.
X, k1, k2, e1, e2, gr, gi = sp.symbols(
    "X k1 k2 e1 e2 g_real g_imag", real=True
)
w1, w2, eps = sp.symbols("omega1 omega2 epsilon", positive=True)
D = sp.diag(w1, w2)
K = sp.diag(k1, k2)
g = gr + sp.I * gi
phase = sp.exp(-sp.I * (k1 - k2) * X)
E = sp.Matrix([[e1, g * phase], [sp.conjugate(g * phase), e2]])
Eprime = E.diff(X)
A = D - eps * E

# 4. Translation covariance and Hermiticity, without choosing real amplitudes.
check(
    "translation_derivative_and_hermiticity",
    [E.H - E, A.H - A, Eprime + sp.I * (K * E - E * K)],
    "E'=−i[K,E]; both the profile and selected frequency generator are Hermitian.",
)

x1, y1, x2, y2 = sp.symbols("x1 y1 x2 y2", real=True)
beta = sp.Matrix([x1 + sp.I * y1, x2 + sp.I * y2])
betadot = -sp.I * A * beta
Qbeta = sp.expand((beta.H * beta)[0])
force = eps * (beta.H * Eprime * beta)[0]

# 5. Norm/action conservation follows from the actual amplitude equation.
Qdot = (betadot.H * beta + beta.H * betadot)[0]
check(
    "smooth_wave_action",
    Qdot,
    "The two-mode canonical equation preserves total Q, including complex phases.",
)

# 6. The field loses exactly the receiver's acquired momentum.
Pcdot = (betadot.H * K * beta + beta.H * K * betadot)[0]
check(
    "smooth_total_momentum",
    Pcdot + force,
    "Pdot_carrier=−epsilon beta†E' beta cancels the moving receiver force.",
)

# 7. Energy includes both recoil and the changing interaction position.
MR = sp.Symbol("rest_energy_R", positive=True)
PR = sp.Symbol("P_R", real=True)
HR = sp.sqrt(MR**2 + c**2 * PR**2)
Xdot = c**2 * PR / HR
Hfdot = (
    betadot.H * A * beta + beta.H * A * betadot
)[0] - eps * (beta.H * Eprime * beta)[0] * Xdot
HRdot = sp.diff(HR, PR) * force
check(
    "smooth_total_energy",
    Hfdot + HRdot,
    "d(Hbody+beta†[D−epsilon E]beta)/dT=0 with exact moving-body recoil.",
)

sigmas = [
    sp.Matrix([[0, 1], [1, 0]]),
    sp.Matrix([[0, -sp.I], [sp.I, 0]]),
    sp.diag(1, -1),
]
Atotal = sp.kronecker_product(A, sp.eye(2))
spin_matrices = [sp.kronecker_product(sp.eye(2), s) for s in sigmas]

# 8. All three spin components commute with the selected spin-independent law.
check(
    "smooth_internal_spin",
    [Atotal * S - S * Atotal for S in spin_matrices],
    "The spatial interaction preserves every internal doublet spin component.",
)

# 9. Derive the sign of the energy current directly from the wave derivatives.
inertia, amplitude = sp.symbols("I_wave amplitude", positive=True)
dbar_dt = sp.I * w * amplitude
dphi_dx = sp.I * k * amplitude
current = -inertia * c**2 * sp.re(dbar_dt * dphi_dx)
density_energy = (
    inertia * amplitude**2 * (w**2 + c**2 * k**2 + w0**2) / 2
)
density_action = inertia * w * amplitude**2
check(
    "single_mode_energy_current",
    [
        current - c**2 * k * density_action,
        current - vg * density_energy,
        density_energy - w * density_action,
    ],
    "j_E=−I c^2 Re(phi_t* phi_x)=c^2 k q=e v_g; its sign follows k.",
)

# 10. Internal energy changes are changes of body inertia, not external add-ons.
Mbare, B, Er, wr = sp.symbols("M_bare B E_record omega_R", positive=True)
Qbound = sp.Symbol("Q_bound", nonnegative=True)
Pbody = sp.Symbol("P_body", real=True)
rest = Mbare * c**2 + B + Er + wr * Qbound
body = sp.sqrt(rest**2 + c**2 * Pbody**2)
check(
    "exact_body_root_and_rest_energy_dependence",
    [
        sp.sqrt(body**2 - c**2 * Pbody**2) - rest,
        sp.diff(body, Pbody) - c**2 * Pbody / body,
        sp.diff(body, B) - rest / body,
        sp.diff(body, Qbound) - wr * rest / body,
    ],
    "Exact body kinematics retains every internal rest-energy contribution.",
)

# 11. Parametrize a strictly positive post-capture buffer, and reconstruct it
# from the proposed event formulas. This is the capacity domain, not an
# assertion that every arbitrary input can be captured.
Bplus = sp.Symbol("B_final", positive=True)
Pplus, Pc = sp.symbols("P_final P_carrier", real=True)
Ec = sp.Symbol("E_carrier", positive=True)
Hint = sp.Symbol("H_interaction", real=True)
rest_capture = Mbare * c**2 + Bplus + wr * Q
Hplus = sp.sqrt(rest_capture**2 + c**2 * Pplus**2)
Hminus_capture = Hplus - (Ec + Hint)
Pminus_capture = Pplus - Pc
root_capture = sp.sqrt(
    (Hminus_capture + Ec + Hint) ** 2
    - c**2 * (Pminus_capture + Pc) ** 2
)
B_capture = sp.simplify(root_capture - Mbare * c**2 - wr * Q)
H_rebuilt_capture = sp.sqrt(
    (Mbare * c**2 + B_capture + wr * Q) ** 2 + c**2 * Pplus**2
)
check(
    "capture_event_energy_momentum_and_buffer",
    [
        B_capture - Bplus,
        H_rebuilt_capture - Hminus_capture - Ec - Hint,
        Pplus - Pminus_capture - Pc,
    ],
    "On the positive final-buffer domain, capture realizes the exact root and "
    "conserves full energy and momentum, including disappearance of H_int.",
)

# 12. Source bound energy is included once inside its initial rest energy.
Bs, Ers, ws = sp.symbols("B_source E_record_source omega_source", positive=True)
ks = sp.Symbol("binding_parameter", positive=True)
kappa = ks / (1 + ks)  # Exact parametrization 0<kappa<1.
Psource = sp.Symbol("P_source_initial", real=True)
rest_source_initial = (
    Mbare * c**2 + Bs + Ers + (1 - kappa) * ws * Q
)
Hsource_initial = sp.sqrt(rest_source_initial**2 + c**2 * Psource**2)
Psource_final = Psource - Pc
rest_source_final = Mbare * c**2 + Bplus
Hsource_final = sp.sqrt(rest_source_final**2 + c**2 * Psource_final**2)
# Label the admitted outgoing energy by the difference; its split into free
# and interaction pieces remains explicit in the conservation substitution.
Hint_birth = Hsource_initial - Hsource_final - Ec
source_root = sp.sqrt(
    (Hsource_initial - (Ec + Hint_birth)) ** 2 - c**2 * Psource_final**2
)
B_source_final = sp.simplify(source_root - Mbare * c**2)
Hsource_rebuilt = sp.sqrt(
    (Mbare * c**2 + B_source_final) ** 2 + c**2 * Psource_final**2
)
check(
    "emission_event_energy_momentum_and_binding",
    [
        B_source_final - Bplus,
        Hsource_rebuilt + Ec + Hint_birth - Hsource_initial,
        Psource_final + Pc - Psource,
        sp.diff(rest_source_initial, Q) - (1 - kappa) * ws,
    ],
    "Emission realizes a positive final source buffer, counts initial binding "
    "once, and conserves energy and momentum including the interaction at birth.",
)

# 13. Derive the moving oscillator's clock rate from Hbody, not from a
# fixed-inertia oscillator formula in laboratory time.
mb, nu = sp.symbols("M_buffer nu_buffer", positive=True)
qb, pb = sp.symbols("q_buffer p_buffer", real=True)
Bosc = pb**2 / (2 * mb) + mb * nu**2 * qb**2 / 2
rest_other = sp.Symbol("other_rest_energy", positive=True)
rest_osc = rest_other + Bosc
Hosc_body = sp.sqrt(rest_osc**2 + c**2 * Pbody**2)
qdot = sp.diff(Hosc_body, pb)
pdot = -sp.diff(Hosc_body, qb)
dilation = rest_osc / Hosc_body
Bdot = sp.diff(Bosc, qb) * qdot + sp.diff(Bosc, pb) * pdot
# chi=atan2(M nu q,p), evaluated away from the zero-energy state.
chidot = mb * nu * (pb * qdot - qb * pdot) / (
    pb**2 + (mb * nu * qb) ** 2
)
check(
    "moving_oscillator_proper_phase_and_energy",
    [
        Bdot,
        qdot - dilation * pb / mb,
        pdot + dilation * mb * nu**2 * qb,
        chidot - nu * dilation,
    ],
    "B is constant but chi_dot=nu Mrest/Hbody=nu/gamma in laboratory time.",
)

# 14. The finite energy change is realized in actual oscillator coordinates.
Bold, Bnew = sp.symbols("B_old B_new", positive=True)
chi = sp.Symbol("chi", real=True)
qold = sp.sqrt(2 * Bold / (mb * nu**2)) * sp.sin(chi)
pold = sp.sqrt(2 * mb * Bold) * sp.cos(chi)
scale = sp.sqrt(Bnew / Bold)
qnew, pnew = scale * qold, scale * pold
check(
    "finite_buffer_reset_energy_and_phase",
    [
        pnew**2 / (2 * mb) + mb * nu**2 * qnew**2 / 2 - Bnew,
        qnew / sp.sqrt(2 * Bnew / (mb * nu**2)) - sp.sin(chi),
        pnew / sp.sqrt(2 * mb * Bnew) - sp.cos(chi),
    ],
    "Positive oscillator scaling realizes B_new and retains both phase coordinates.",
)

# 15. A common normalized internal polarization factors out of all spatial
# modes, and copying that whole packet between owners preserves action/spin.
theta, phi = sp.symbols("theta phi", real=True)
u = sp.Matrix(
    [sp.cos(theta / 2), sp.exp(sp.I * phi) * sp.sin(theta / 2)]
)
field_spinor = sp.kronecker_product(beta, u)
Qfield = (field_spinor.H * field_spinor)[0]
factor_residuals = [(u.H * u)[0] - 1]
for sigma, Sigma in zip(sigmas, spin_matrices):
    spin_field = (field_spinor.H * Sigma * field_spinor)[0] / 2
    spin_factor = Qbeta * (u.H * sigma * u)[0] / 2
    factor_residuals.append(spin_field - spin_factor)
    Sbound_before = sp.Symbol("owner_spin_component", real=True)
    # Capture: carrier vanishes; owner receives its unchanged polarization.
    factor_residuals.append(
        (Sbound_before + spin_factor) - (Sbound_before + spin_field)
    )
    # Emission is the reverse ownership transfer.
    factor_residuals.append(
        (Sbound_before - spin_factor + spin_field) - Sbound_before
    )
Qowner = sp.Symbol("owner_action", nonnegative=True)
factor_residuals.extend(
    [
        (Qowner + Qbeta) - (Qowner + Qfield),
        (Qowner - Qbeta + Qfield) - Qowner,
    ]
)
check(
    "polarization_factorization_and_owner_transfer",
    factor_residuals,
    "The full carrier spin is Q u†sigma u/2; complete-packet transfer preserves "
    "all spin components and total action while changing ownership.",
)


def main() -> int:
    passed = sum(item["passed"] for item in CHECKS)
    payload = {
        "model": "Active finite-band carrier, symbolic verification",
        "sympy_version": sp.__version__,
        "summary": {"checks": len(CHECKS), "passed": passed, "failed": len(CHECKS) - passed},
        "assumptions": [
            "Positive c, omega0, packet action and bare scales; finite Hermitian mode matrices.",
            "Constant continuous-segment coupling and E'(X)=-i[K,E(X)].",
            "Spatial coupling acts identically on both internal-spin components.",
            "One common flat-channel time; spin comparisons are in the selected common frame.",
            "Physical pre-event bodies and positive final buffers: the event checks "
            "parametrize this domain and do not certify arbitrary-input capacity.",
            "Emission interaction energy is its actual post-creation value, included once.",
            "No trajectory integration, finite-band refinement or signal-front claim "
            "is tested by this symbolic script.",
        ],
        "checks": CHECKS,
    }
    output = Path(__file__).with_name("symbolic_results.json")
    output.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({"output": str(output), **payload["summary"]}))
    if passed != len(CHECKS):
        for item in CHECKS:
            if not item["passed"]:
                print(item["name"], item["nonzero_residuals"])
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
